title: Standardize subnet tagging, AZ assignment and EIP lifecycle for multi-az VPCs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Over time multiple teams have added ad-hoc subnet modules and scripts that created private/public subnets with inconsistent Availability Zone placement, tag conventions (Name, environment, role), and various Elastic IP (EIP) allocation strategies. This has caused terraform drift, cross-account naming collisions, and manual steps during failovers. Goal: refactor Terraform infra so that subnets and associated NAT/EIP resources follow a single convention per VPC, and provide a zero-downtime migration path for existing workspaces.
acceptance_criteria: All VPCs use the new module interface for subnet creation (env_subnet_count, az_allocation_strategy)
EIP allocation is managed by a single nat_gateway module with deterministic naming to avoid duplicate allocations in the same account/region
Terraform plan in staging shows no destructive changes for existing resources after state migration and import steps
Automated tests validate AZ distribution, route table associations, and tag presence
Runbooks updated and migration script archived in repo with one-click instructions
technical_notes: Primary changes: 1) Introduce modules/networking/subnet-v2 with explicit az_assignment and stable resource naming; 2) Replace per-stack ad-hoc nat_gateway resources with modules/networking/nat-manager that creates zero-to-n NAT Gateways backed by an EIP pool; 3) Upgrade hashicorp/aws provider to v5.2 in modules and root stacks to take advantage of the new local AZ data source semantics and avoid implicit AZ name differences; 4) Add a terraform state import shim to map old resource addresses to new ones to preserve continuity.
implementation_plan: Design new module interfaces and update module registry entry
Create nat-manager module that supports single EIP-per-nat naming and idempotent replace policy
Add automated acceptance tests in terratest/kitchen for subnet tag assertions
Upgrade provider versions in a branch and run full plan against staging workspace
Iteratively migrate one non-critical VPC (staging) with state import script and validate
Rollout to production VPCs in small batches with runbook and rollback steps
migration_steps: Create backup of terraform state in S3 and snapshot DynamoDB lock table
Run terraform init with new modules and provider pinned to 5.2.0 in a staging workspace
Run migration script tools/tf-migrate/map-old-to-new.sh to generate import commands
Run terraform import for each discovered resource in staging workspace
Run terraform plan and confirm zero-diff for resources that were only address-renamed
Apply in staging and run terratest acceptance suite
Schedule maintenance windows for prod VPCs and repeat import + apply with one VPC at a time
test_plan: Unit: validate module variable schema and example configurations
Integration: run terratest suite to assert AZ distribution, routes and nat behavior
E2E: spin up ephemeral cluster that uses new subnet tags and ensure service endpoints route correctly
Chaos: simulate AZ failure and verify NAT reassignment and EIP continuity
Preflight: run terraform plan in every workspace and verify no unexpected resource replacements
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal review, docs, and dry-run in sandbox account
Phase 1: Staging VPC migration with smoke tests (1 day)
Phase 2: Prod low-risk VPCs (non-customer-facing) with monitoring thresholds
Phase 3: High-traffic VPCs during scheduled maintenance window; on-call engineer assigned
Fallback: use state snapshots to revert terraform state and recreate old resources if import fails
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: Initial design doc shared with infra team and PM; feedback to prefer deterministic naming over tags-only lookups
2025-03-04: Prototype nat-manager created; verified deterministic EIP naming in account sandbox
2025-03-06: Provider upgrade tested locally against mock AZs; discovered change in az ordering semantics requiring explicit az list in module
2025-03-09: Migration script (map-old-to-new.sh) landed in feature branch for internal review (PR #1126)
2025-03-12: Ran import on staging VPC; one route table needed manual reconciliation due to earlier human-created entry. Updated script to handle that case.

notes_for_review: Watch outs: provider upgrade can change default behaviour for az lookup which affects existing stacks with hardcoded az indices. Ensure SRE on-call is paged during prod imports. Keep EIP quota checks in preflight. Aim to avoid creating transient EIPs that will increase cost.
